newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK yachtsmen to dump British Queen for new patron.
newsitem.headline: HK yachtsmen to dump British Queen for new patron.

text.p: The elite Royal Hong Kong Yacht Club plans to jettison Britain's Queen Elizabeth in favour of a new mainland patron to reflect the territory's handover to China, the club said on Wednesday.

"I will be liaising with Hong Kong's future chief executive, Tung Chee-hwa, to determine the most appropriate way for the club to be patronised by the new sovereign power," club commodore David Kong said in a letter sent to club members, a copy of which was made available to Reuters.

Tung was selected as chief executive under Beijing's auspices in December 1996 to take the helm in the territory when it reverts to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 after more than 150 years of British rule.
Kong said the club, which has been a pillar of colonial high society, would also change its logo, which incorporates the Union Jack, and adopt a new flag.
The Royal Hong Kong Yacht Club planned to hold an extraordinary meeting on June 12 to approve the registration of a Chinese business name, he said.
The club, whose members voted last year to keep the "Royal" tag on its name, would undertake the changes "in anticipation of the forthcoming change in sovereignty", Kong said.
The club would make as little change as possible and whatever action it took would comply with international nautical etiquette, he said.
Symbols of British colonialism in Hong Kong are quickly fading out at the approach of the sovereignty transfer.
The "Royal" tag has been dropped by the Hong Kong Jockey Club and the Hong Kong Golf Club.
The queen's portrait has also been removed from stamps and coins in favour of the territory's famous harbour skyline.
